externalTitle: Policies, processes, procedures and practices for AI risk; Accountability structures
notes: GOVERN establishes organisational AI risk governance. AIDCF GOV-01 adds decision rights over infrastructure Assurance Decisions, committee oversight of gates and methodology ownership.

externalTitle: Accountability structures
notes: Roles, responsibilities and lines of communication for AI risk overlap RACI and role ownership. Critical-function accountability for facility and AI infrastructure and evidence custody are AIDCF-specific.

externalTitle: Policies, processes, procedures and practices for AI risk
notes: Policy coverage overlaps; Technical Standard Baselines and exception governance for engineering standards are not addressed.

externalTitle: Policies and risk tolerance; Prioritisation of and response to assessed AI risks
notes: Risk tolerance and prioritised risk response align with Risk Appetite Linkage. The AI RMF has no Critical Gate concept.

externalTitle: Policies (legal and regulatory requirements); Engagement with relevant AI actors
notes: GOVERN 1.1 (legal and regulatory requirements understood and managed) and GOVERN 5 (engagement with external AI actors) overlap stakeholder and regulatory interface.

externalTitle: Training; Workforce diversity and team composition; Independent assessors in measurement
notes: Training and independent assessment (MEASURE 1.3) overlap competence and independence. Conflict management and appeal are not addressed.

externalTitle: Inventory of AI systems
notes: GOVERN 1.6 calls for an inventory of AI systems. AIDCF CAP-01 registers infrastructure Capability Instances; the AI system inventory can be linked as the demand-side consumer.

externalTitle: Context established; AI capabilities, targeted usage and goals understood
notes: Intended purpose and expected benefits of the AI system frame which infrastructure Service Outcomes matter; tolerances are not defined.

externalTitle: Context established; Impacts characterised
notes: Likelihood and magnitude of impacts inform criticality and stakeholder consequence; infrastructure impact tolerance is not defined.

externalTitle: Decommissioning and phasing out AI systems
notes: GOVERN 1.7 addresses safe decommissioning of AI systems; AIDCF CAP-06 addresses design-to-operation traceability, commissioning acceptance and retirement of infrastructure capability.

externalTitle: Risks and benefits mapped for all components, including third-party
notes: Component-level risk mapping is the AI-system analogue of dependency discovery; upstream facility, recovery-only and downstream consequence paths are not addressed.

externalTitle: Third-party software, data and supply-chain risk; Management of third-party AI risks
notes: Third-party AI risk overlaps external provider dependency. Utility and telecom dependency are outside scope.

externalTitle: Contingency processes for third-party failures
notes: GOVERN 6.2 contingency for failures in high-risk third-party data or systems is a context for substitution readiness; concentration analysis is not addressed.

externalTitle: Context established
notes: Context-setting informs boundaries but defines no assessment, provider or tenant boundary.

externalTitle: Management of third-party AI risks
notes: Regular monitoring of third-party resources overlaps provider performance review; dependency health indicators and revalidation are not addressed.

aidcfFamilyName: Fire, life safety and emergency interfaces

externalTitle: Evaluation of trustworthy characteristics (environmental impact)
notes: MEASURE 2.12 asks that environmental impact and sustainability of AI training and management be assessed and documented. AIDCF ENV-02 requires measured facility energy performance (PUE, allocation, efficiency under load).

externalTitle: Evaluation of trustworthy characteristics (environmental impact)
notes: Environmental impact assessment may include water; no WUE or water-scarcity response requirements.

externalTitle: Evaluation of trustworthy characteristics (environmental impact)
notes: Environmental impact documentation is a context for carbon accounting; boundary, energy-attribute evidence and reporting traceability are not addressed.

externalTitle: Evaluation in deployment (functionality and behaviour monitored); Post-deployment monitoring
notes: Production monitoring of AI system behaviour sits above accelerator and node health telemetry; it can surface symptoms of infrastructure degradation.

externalTitle: Accountability structures (training)
notes: AI-risk training; no operational staffing or authorisation requirements.

externalTitle: Risk treatments, response and recovery, and communication
notes: MANAGE 4.3 (incidents and errors communicated and tracked) is a context for incident and problem management of AI systems, not of facility infrastructure.

externalTitle: Tracking identified AI risks over time
notes: Tracking risk over time; no capacity review or service-level monitoring.

externalTitle: Strategies to maximise benefit and minimise negative impact (supersede, disengage, deactivate)
notes: MANAGE 2.4 mechanisms to disengage or deactivate AI systems relate to graceful degradation at the AI-system layer.

externalTitle: Contingency processes for third-party failures
notes: Contingency for third-party failure is one input to continuity strategy.

externalTitle: Risk treatments, including response and recovery
notes: Response and recovery for AI risks; no infrastructure recovery sequencing or configuration restoration.

externalTitle: Evaluation of trustworthy characteristics (security and resilience)
notes: MEASURE 2.7 evaluates AI system security and resilience; AIDCF RES-05 requires component, integrated scenario and tabletop tests of infrastructure.

externalTitle: Communication plans
notes: Communication of risk treatments; crisis command not addressed.

externalTitle: Third-party software, data and supply-chain risk
notes: Policies for third-party AI risk overlap supplier due diligence at objective level.

externalTitle: Third-party software, data and supply-chain risk
notes: Third-party risk policies (including intellectual property) are a context for contracts; evidence rights and exit rights are not specified.

externalTitle: Supply-chain risk; Component risk mapping
notes: No hardware provenance or counterfeit-prevention requirements.

externalTitle: Third-party software risk; Monitoring of pre-trained models and third-party resources
notes: Third-party software monitoring is a context for firmware and update supply; signature validation and release provenance are not addressed.

externalTitle: Evaluation of trustworthy characteristics (security and resilience)
notes: AI system security evaluation; no security telemetry or forensic readiness for infrastructure.

externalTitle: Human-AI configurations and oversight; Human oversight processes defined; Mechanisms to supersede, disengage or deactivate
notes: Human oversight and deactivation of AI systems overlap AIDCF SEC-06 objectives. AIDCF adds bounded authority, approval controls, command allowlisting and safe rollback for AI or automation acting on infrastructure.

externalTitle: Policies, processes, procedures and practices (transparency and documentation)
notes: Documentation expectations; no evidence taxonomy or repository requirements.

externalTitle: Appropriate methods and metrics; Test sets, metrics and tools documented
notes: Documenting TEVV methods supports evidence relevance and reliability; provenance and custody are not addressed.

externalTitle: Appropriate methods and metrics identified and applied
notes: Selection of methods and metrics and involvement of independent assessors overlap assessment planning.

externalTitle: Risks not measured documented; Risk tracking; Feedback on measurement efficacy
notes: MEASURE 1.1 asks that risks that cannot be measured be documented, which parallels UNKNOWN preservation. The AI RMF has no UNKNOWN severity or decision effect.

externalTitle: Determination whether the AI system achieves its purpose and whether deployment should proceed
notes: MANAGE 1.1 go/no-go determination parallels the Assurance Decision. Gate applicability, gate evidence floors and bounded claim language are AIDCF-specific.

externalTitle: Ongoing monitoring and periodic review; Post-deployment monitoring
notes: Periodic review and post-deployment monitoring overlap continuing assurance; evidence expiry and decision suspension are AIDCF-specific.
